messages:
arya: Quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA kernel selection RFC — noticed some odd perf curves on the canary cluster during the 10k client burst test. p95 latency spiked on mixed-length workloads.

sam: Saw that too. Short summary of numbers from the run:
- baseline (always-GQA): 1200 tok/s, p95 42ms
- hybrid heuristic v1: 1520 tok/s, p95 89ms (regression for short queries)
- always-MQA for short-only: 1800 tok/s, p95 30ms

lin: Important detail: the hybrid v1 hit a lot of kernel switch overheads when a single batch contained 1 long seq + many short seqs. GQA path did extra KV merges which serialized the batch.

jordan: I think this is the KV cache coalescing problem we flagged earlier — when queries of different seq lengths share a batch we do expensive pad/trim ops. Memory churn also increases.

mika: Can we surface a tiny heuristic at the scheduler so we avoid mixed-length batches that would force a switch? e.g., prefer grouping by seq-length bucket first, then by kernel preference.

lin: Yes, prototype scoring I used:
```
// per-batch score, higher => prefer MQA
score = w_len * mean_query_len
        + w_short * fraction_short
        - w_kv * estimated_kv_merge_cost
        + w_batch * log(batch_size)
```
Adjust weights per model. The problem is estimating estimated_kv_merge_cost cheaply. We used a constant multiplier based on distinct cache keys in batch.

sam: For rollout we hit two failure modes: 1) scheduler flapped decisions across consecutive micro-batches (causing jitter), 2) fallback path to fallback-kernel (torch) wasn't instrumented so we lost visibility.

runtime-bot: [alert] rollout/hybrid-v1: p95-latency > 80ms for 12m — triggered autoscale and route-fallbacks.

arya: Proposal: 3-part plan
1) Move kernel selection into the Scheduler decision point with an explicit "sticky" policy for X ms per session to avoid flapping.
2) Add a cheap KV-compatibility check: if estimated_kv_merge_cost > threshold OR batch is high-variance seq-length, prefer pure GQA or split the batch.
3) Instrument fallback path and add metrics: kernel_selected, kernel_switched, kv_merge_est, batch_variance.

jordan: Sticky policy seems right. Suggest sticky TTL be proportional to observed session variance: low var sessions get longer stickiness. TTL config example: { "sticky_ttl_ms": 200, "multiplier_if_low_var": 4 }.

lin: For splitting batches we should avoid full copy semantics. Implementation sketch: a two-pass batcher that first computes seq-length histogram, then emits sub-batches where possible without copying token buffers; instead emit index views. That keeps zero-copy on GPU where we can.

mika: Rollout steps:
- stage A: enable instrumentation only on canaries (1 cluster)
- stage B: enable sticky selection + histogram batching on 10% traffic
- stage C: enable full heuristic (kv check) on 50% after 48h if no regressions

sam: Need to record guardrail metrics for user-facing p99 and tokens/sec and also internal metrics: kernel_switch_rate and avg_kv_merge_cost. Add an alert if kernel_switch_rate > 0.02 per minute.

arya: Decision for now: implement sticky selection + seq-length histogram batching + instrumentation. Defer kv-cost tuned heuristic until we have better signal. Action items:
- lin: prototype zero-copy sub-batching (ETA 3 days)
- sam: add kernel metrics and alert rules (ETA 2 days)
- mika: prepare rollout playbook and canary config (ETA 1 day)
- jordan: run mem-frag microbench and share numbers (ETA 4 days)

runtime-bot: noted. Created tasks: #INF-2412, #INF-2413, #INF-2414.

arya: Thanks — let's sync next Tue after the first canary run. :thumbsup:
